english: Stepping into the hidden tomb, you see a colorful display of twinkling light through the gloomy and dusty air.
An eerie altar. Placed on top: a skull and several colorful gems.
Valuable too.
Like, extremely valuable. But probably horrendously cursed sadly.
And shiny! Take one. You could get it appraised by someone downtown...
The skull is a sign of death.
Mm. Don't touch anything.
Whatever esoteric effect is in place here - do not disturb it.
(Grab a gemstone.)
(Grab the skull.)
(Just look around.)
One of which you are holding in your hand.
Sweet! This must be invaluable.
Uh oh. That was probably a really, really stupid idea.
Your companion stares at the gem in your hand, stuttering out a few words.
Y-you just...!
You walk into a creepy tomb and just...?
Oh. What is that... feeling?
Darkness is coursing down your arm.
A searing pain takes hold.
Causing you to drop the gem.
But the gem does not hit the floor.
Gods be damned...
The goblin takes a step back.
You watch it levitate in front of you, as the pain subsides in your arm.
That is a curse of needles.
That is a curse. Of some kind.
The treasure on the shrine must be heavily enchanted.
(Try to grab the floating gem. Again.)
Ouch.
(Take a step back.) "Floating cursed gem. I hate these."
As your fingers touch the surface, they immediately repel back.
Stop touching it!
You fool! He slaps your hand away.
Just be happy you didn't lose a hand.
Slowly you watch as the gem moves through the dusty air towards the shrine.
Until it lands in the exact same place you picked it up from.
It's for the best, Cleric.
Don't forget, anything you grab down here is taxed by both the Halfways and your precious city.
WHAT?
Terrifying.
(Just stare at the returned gem.)
Taxes, Cleric.
You know. The Tithehouse.
Not something you've had to deal with before, but yes.
The Tithehouse demands a 40% cut on all collected goods in the City Below the City.
Sure. But not even official delvers report everything.
It's not like they can keep track of each ancient coin and relic.
Those taxes go to a good cause. The city offers many free services to its people, that would not be possible if a heavy cut was not imposed on all types of income.
It also pays for your salary.
There's a TAX on TREASURE?!
Right. There's a tax on loot.
Good. The city needs those taxes.
He holds up a claw. "Then Lady Sageleaf imposes another fifty percent cut on any reclaimed goods in the Tolstad Tunnels."
But... but...
You'll be left with NOTHING!
Except if you're an official delver, of course. Then you'll get away with 10%.
FASCISTS!
A wise scheme. Incentivizes adventurers to not go behind the backs of the goblins.
Either risk getting caught by Sageleaf, or accept a tiny cut?
The goblins do not have official jurisdiction on any piece of the City Below.
Such actions are way beyond their powers.
Why would anyone do anything if the spoils are split by some overbearing specter of filthy socialism?
That doesn't seem fair.
Good. I love paying more than half of my income to people who didn't do any work.
The goblin shrugs. "You live in Norvik, Cleric. I didn't choose it. I'm guessing you didn't really either."
But still we live here. So taxes are paid.
I'm talking about the goblin cut.
Fair point.
You're going to pull the genocide card? Really?
Maybe we should abolish taxes...
Ah. Well, you can see that as a payback for the whole genocide, then.
He quips, but there's a tone of seriousness behind his voice.
Sure is.
If it works, it works.
Hey, anything's possible. Who knows what the next election cycle will bring.
Abolish taxes. Legalize murder. Sanctify cunnilingus.
Sounds good. I'd vote for you.
The second one seems a bit harsh.
What's that third one?
Ah yes. A real goblin party. The slogan would be We Love Anarchy, and we'll win by a landslide.
Obviously.
Anyway. The shrine...
Hey, would be a blast from the past. We used to be fair game, didn't we?
He's talking about the Goblin Genocide. A terrible period of Urthfolk history.
I'm sorry for that.
Right. (Turn away and look at the shrine.)
He holds up his palm. "Don't. Just- just look at the shrine, okay?"
The goblin clears his throat.
It's a- it's a sex thing, Cleric.
About this shrine... (Quickly change the subject.)
He points at you. "Sarcasm?"
Yes.
No.
Actually no.
He takes a breath, then asks again. "Sarcasm?"
Got it. I'm trying to learn your, you know, mannerisms.
Carry on.
The shrine is quiet. The colorful gems cover its altar, as well as the eye sockets of the central skull.
To think this sacrilegious and quite frankly ominous corner would be stashed away in such a holy place.
This is Urth's original crypt, for gods' sake! Is there no depth of depravity these cultists and undeath-enthusiasts can stoop to?
Your legs wobble as you look upon it.
You should pray to this thing. It is stronger than you.
E-I should just leave this alone. For now.
The goblin squints.
A bit? Depends on what type of skull it is, I suppose.
Look at the jaw. It's all wonky. And the eyes?
I suppose we should not judge the look of a bejeweled skull, for entirely egalitarian reasons.
Nah. It's probably just a human with unfortunate aesthetics.
He sighs.
Look at you, being all saint-like all of a sudden.
But to be fair...
He nods.
I don't like ripping on a dead guy, but... yeah.
That's one wacky skull.
A <shake>WACKY</shake> skull?!
You GOD DAMNED phrenologists!
You obviously should not do that.
Yeah. At least while this goblin is watching.
Don't want to deal with those taxes.
You're right. I shouldn't.
What if I crush the skull first? I could probably smash it.
You say that you shouldn't. But I have a sneaking suspicion that's not what you're thinking up there in that helm of yours.
So your plan is to just smash the clearly super cursed skull on the obviously evil altar.
I knew you'd be like this.
The goblin takes a step back and gives you a polite bow.
Be my guest.
Thank you, Snell. I'll crush the skull now. (Give him a thumbs up.)
The <shake>FUCK</shake> you will!
They do...
But even such a valuable doesn't override your self-preservation, in this case.
Maybe if you're quick enough...?
DO NOT.
Mm. Do not consider such a foolish action.
The <shake>FUCK</shake> are you SHOUTING for?!
Wait, wait...!
The second you place your hand on the top of the skull, the gems begin to glow.
A blast of necrotic energy fills your veins from your palm, going up to your heart.
Despite this, you CANNOT remove the palm.
It is GLUED to the skull.
Stop, Cleric! Stop!
(Scream and shake the skull.)
As you do, a shriek fills the air.
Followed by a shrill voice.
PUT. ME. <shake>DOWN</shake>!
(Keep shaking.)
After two more shakes, the skull pops out of your palm, the necrotic damage on your flesh fading.
The skull bounces against the wall, before stopping suddenly mid-air.
As if lifted by some invisible force, the bejeweled skull rises from the altar.
Its gleaming eyes twinkling in the light, its jaw chattering. The noise causes you to recoil.
DEATH.
No way.
An unending wave of dread falls upon your essence.
An esoteric force. It...
It is entering your mind.
U-undead abomination!
(Try to run.)
Urth protect me.
Protect you?!
The goblin tries to grab you, but he freezes and groans.
What the hell...?!
He falls to his knees.
You barely stand.
I... can't move...
The DREAD is overbearing.
The DREAD- you resist it.
The skull's jaw stops chattering.
As the noise disappears, you feel in-control once more.
Slightly.
You wake me up for some trifling bullshit? You a Trifler, huh?
It clicks its teeth together.
No, sir. Please stop making that sound.
W-what's Trifling?
I'm The Cleric. (Try not to puke.)
I'm a... rogue.
I'm a great wizard, nothing else! (Wobble a bit.)
I make any damn sound I like, you hear?
It's what you're doing, <shake>mortal</shake>!
You're trifling like a Trifler!
CLERIC, EH?
That does sound like triflings to me!
No! It's different!
Yeah, that's fair. Please don't kill me.
I'll bet your soul it's not!
That's what I like- GR-rrrr-OVEL FOR ME!
The skull floats closer to you, causing you to convulse on the spot.
A WIZARD?!
It looks you up and down.
Hah! You're but a pup tangled in Strings.
A CLERIC lost in Jor's tangles...!
A Cleric...! Of a DEAD god...!
Holy hells, this thing is terrible.
Just being close to it ruins your posture.
The body cannot sustain this... undeath.
The skull lets out howling laughter as it shudders about in the air.
I am NECROLORD BONDAVOL!
Wah-ha-ha!
Punch. The. Skull.
Necrolord? That is a title of Old Diminor.
You've been unfortunate enough to encounter here a remnant of the Arcanists - left to decay into this mad form.
A Demi-Lich.
A horrifying creature. A Lich, fallen into a state of insanity and decay, rotting into nothing but a skull.
It is in many ways the dangerous variant, for its madness is as unpredictable as it is dangerous.
PUNCH. THE. SKULL.
You're a...!
This is a...!
Punch the skull.
A great and horrifying lich! Yes!
He does not consider himself decayed. A sign of madness.
Yes, it is my DOOM!
Probably yours too.
I heard him!
Yeah! It's pretty clear!
The goblin looks horrified and ready to spring into action, despite the shaking legs.
A scared little <shake>mortal</shake>? Yessss...!
He's enjoying this way too much.
No trouble?
Boring.
BORING?!
Hey, screw this guy!
Boring? What do you want me to do, look for trouble? Be an asshole?
Sorry?
Hey, fuck you buddy!
At least that'd be interesting.
Wimp.
I said, you're BOOOORING!
That's the spirit!
Be abrasive! Don't let anyone tug you along!
That's what it's all about!
A blinding light emits from your gloved hand as you twist the Strings around the air of the horrifying skull.
(Turn all undead in the chamber.)
It lets out a high-pitched scream and slams against the wall.
Before falling down to the altar, still.
Holy shit, the goblin mutters and lifts his gaze.
Did you... get it?
Of course not!
Then you see it rattle upon the table. It rises once again, its jaw slightly unhinged.
The skull rises once again, its jaw slightly unhinged.
Did you think that would destroy ME?!
You channel the dark energy through your palm, reaching towards the floating skull.
Necrotic power surges from your fingertips. But...
Ohoho...!
The skull's jaw drops open wide as the negative energy courses into it.
Rather than recoiling, it seems to... drink it in.
Mmm! <shake>DELICIOUS!</shake>
The gems in its eye sockets flare with renewed intensity.
You think such PUNY MAGIC would even scratch someone like me?!
The skull lets out a shrieking cackle, spinning wildly in the air.
But your hand trembles. The spell fizzles at your fingertips.
Come on...
Huh?
You... you attempt to INFLICT WOUNDS on ME?!
The skull rattles with mocking laughter as the wisps of failed necrotic energy dissipate.
You wind up your fist.
Lock eyes with the cursed gemstones in the skull's sockets.
And pray.
Urth be <shake>BLESSED</shake>.
You make contact with the bony surface, sending the abomination spinning in the air.
<shake>Gah...!</shake>
As it stops spinning, it looks at you, askew, and clacks its teeth together.
You strike... at ME?!
The skull lets out a crazed laugh.
Then you attempt to lock eyes with the... gems.
And try to send your shaking arms forward.
Come on, come on...
You... you attempt to strike at ME?!
The skull lets out a mocking laughter as you recover from your missed attack.
I LIKE YOU!
What?
Such gusto! You remind me of my old lieutenant.
That boy always swung at his superiors. I raised him a dozen times over the course of the war!
Stop laughing, I'm trying to kill you, you- undead monster!
Does that mean you won't kill me?
He laughs some more.
Kill? Bit too late for that, you whelp!
Eh.
I do not make promises.
I think so too. Play along now.
If you keep this up, you might be worthy enough to be raised as a servant one day.
The skull stops.
Visken?
What are you, an apprentice?
No?
Yes?
A slave then?
No way. I don't approve of slavery.
More or less, I suppose.
I prefer the term 'servant'.
I sense <shake>sarcasm</shake> here.
Uh-huh. What kind of apprentice?
Tell him you're a... you're a dentist-in-training. That should work.
Officially Visken is a mortician. So...
The esoteric kind?
He's teaching me mortuary stuff.
Dentistry?
I'm not really an apprentice.
Visken doesn't take on Arcane students.
So you're the first embalming student he's taken on, ever? No way, hombre.
He hasn't dealt in that horrid practice for years!
He... started it up again?
I don't believe you.
Hold on. Are you that Cleric looking to speak with the dead elf?
Yes. Obviously?
How did you know that?
No. (Look shifty.)
Obviously.
Yes you are!
He rattles a laugh, slowly spinning in the air.
Visken let me know all about your little situation.
Of course!
The demi-lich clicks once.
You're not very necromantically entangled, are you?
Is that a bad thing?
Not really, no.
I never managed to master that school at Towers.
And thank the gods for that. Foul, filthy magic that is.
Of course it is! Every spellcaster should aim towards the necromantic. It's just natural!
I can see that.
Master it?
No one masters it, not even after centuries of scholarship.
Necromancy is a beautiful art, you knave!
You see, I'm not just some horny wizard...!
The skull drops down and flips around on the table.
I'm a god damned <wiggle>MAAAGE</wiggle>!
You hear the goblin groaning.
This lich is, surprisingly, not a threat.
For whatever reason, his intentions are far more sinister: he intends to teach you something.
Trained in the Arts by Haagin-Dim legends, sent to fight on behalf of the grrrrreatest empire in the history of Jor's arseprint!
Necrolord is not just some title- it's a calling! A dream!
A dream of undead supremacy...! One day it will be reached.
You're the lucky one here. For I will help guide you to a STRING ATTUNEMENT!
A NECROMANTIC attunement!
You'll do that for me?
...Why should I want to learn necromancy?
You and your cursed, esoteric existence is an abomination. You must be destroyed.
Right. Sure, I just have some questions first.
Of course! I owe it to Visken for one.
And for second... I just love spreading the joy of death-magic.
As any sane man would!
This skull is not sane, nor a man.
Agreed.
For one, you'll be able to cast Speak with Dead without trouble.
You'll also gain an appreciation of the subtle art of death-magic. Doesn't that sound lovely?
Sure.
Yes. It does.
No. It really doesn't.
Good!
Yes indeed...
You're wrong. But if you change your mind...
The skull laughs.
Yeah, yeah. Go on about it till you croak.
I've got a Finger of Death here that says your ass is mine, if I want it.
He laughs.
Then talk.
The skull is not going to kill you.
But you do not have the strength to vanquish a demi-lich like this. So...
Later. Do it later.
The skull floats in front of you with a permanent smirk and wide jeweled eyes.
<shake>CLERIC</shake>!
So l-
So loud.
Yeah, that.
So loud.
I will attune with Necromancy.
How did you end up like that?
Tell me about Visken.
E-"I'm going now. Goodbye, Bondavol."
Ah, you never asked did you?
I'm a terrifying lich, of course!
Got it.
You'd have to be pretty STUPID not to!
Nah.
Inter planar travel is overrated.
Go ask Visken. That bastard keeps poking at Jor's relics.
He's into that shit.
For WHAT?
I'm going to ask the local sphinx to turn it into a key for me to enter the Beyond. Through the Pillar of Jor.
I can't tell you... it's a secret... (Be mysterious.)
Then no.
Oh. Well in that case, I'm going to ask the local sphinx to turn it into a key for me to enter the Beyond. Through the Pillar of Jor.
Come on... please... (Beg in an annoying tone of voice.)
Okay, fine.
That sounds absolutely crazy!
You will die by following such a road.
Great!
He grabs the emerald with his teeth - making a clicky noise - then tosses it into your chest.
Go wild!
You genuinely feel an appreciation towards this insanely stupid skull.
You are unsure if this guy ever was smart, or if this is just his mind slipping in his undeath fugue state.
Either way, a win for you.
Now: to return to the sphinx.
The skull does a little dance.
The Strings are always different for each school. Aesthetically speaking.
Everyone views them differently. Abjuration to me is steel. Evocation is lightning.
Necromancy is flesh. Perhaps that can help.
This mad demi-lich offers you knowledge. You do not need it.
Show him. Of course you can attune to necromancy, easily. You're a genius. You can attune to any magic known to man or beyond.
Do you remember?
Yes... I remember that course in school.
Yes. All clerics underwent the Undeath Control class.
They focused mostly on hostile destruction of undeath. Not so much on the management of it.
But the teacher cast an animation spell to create a zombie for you all to train on.
The Strings... they were pale. Like death. (Hold out a hand towards the skull.)
Yes... try it.
He giggles. In that sort of insane, creepy way.
There are many Strings.
Twist this one.
(Twist the String.)
You do so.
And...
The String... grows dark. Black as night.
It flies into your chest.
(Scream and convulse.)
Oh gods...
You fall to your knees. They are weak.
They cannot help him now, goblin.
You did something alright!
(Get up and groan.)
You tossed a ton of negative energy right into your damn heart.
First time I've seen someone do that and live. Impressive!
You are alive, are you? Not a zombie or something behind that thing on your head?
I'm alive. I think.
Fuck you.
(Mumble something incoherent.)
That's the spirit.
Try again later, you'll get it eventually!
Maybe you should rest first. Or something.
He sounds worried. He should be.
Don't throw yourself into doom like this. Can't you figure out something to make it easier?
You understand it better now- now that you've seen the pale String.
Think.
This demi-lich believes himself to be your teacher here.
He might be insane, but there is still knowledge to be had. If you can decipher it.
(Hold out a hand.) "Tell me as best as you can- the School of Necromancy, how do I master it?"
Strings are Strings.
They are equal, but different. You must have seen them a lot. Since you have them running through your flesh in the masses.
I do?
I do.
He continues, "A String of Necromancy becomes that when it intersects with negative energy. Thus it begins to 'look' like flesh to me, for example."
I have surely as many Strings going through my existence as you do. Except mine are Necromantic.
Yours are...
The skull shakes a bit. "Many others. How do you deal with Strings, usually?"
When I attune with Strings, I twist them.
Ah. So that is how you cast your organized spells, then.
Necromancy is special because of that negative energy. Twisting a necromantic String would hurt, naturally, if you are anything but not-alive.
A living necromancer learns to either manage the pain, through mutilation, religious fervor, physical numbness, or...
They learn to cut the String.
...Cut?
Everyone uses different terminology. You might have heard it called 'willing' the String. Or 'Mastering' it.
It's the step every spellcaster must go through to reach the higher tier magic. They must learn to manipulate the String's shape.
The shape of the String?
But it doesn't have a shape? It's just a... dot?
The skull laughs mockingly. "Why do you think they call it a String then, dumb-ass?"
It measures change. Over time.
You might have grabbed and twisted your Strings in the moment, but cutting a String means: grabbing it independently! From ALL its other parts. In the past. And in the future.
Don't just twist it. Separate it from itself.
Oh.
So that's what that means.
<shake>Of course!</shake>
The talk about mastering Strings... it all makes sense now.
The String goes through time.
Manipulating it more closely requires it to be twisted only in the now. Without the other baggage.
(Stick out your hand.)
Yes...
(Locate a String near Bondavol. A pale String.)
Yes...!
(Twist it.)
Ah shit.
(Open your eyes.)
That hurts.
You twisted the String into a Cure Wounds, you idiot. Hurt like a... what do you say- motherfucker!
I failed?
The skull laughs, intensely.
You did great, Cleric. Or should I say, Necromancer?
That was a Cure Wounds, for sure. But a necromantic Cure Wounds.
Instead of a Cure Wounds cast through sissy Abjuration or hardcore flesh-melding Transmutation, you now managed to simply remove the negative energy to reach the same conclusion: healing.
Although yes, it did hurt like all hells. Since negative energy obviously is kind of my thing here, as a glorious lich.
Oh. So I mastered necromancy?
An overstatement perhaps, but you should be able to cast the one spell you're looking for at least.
<shake>Speak with Dead!</shake>
Finally.
That's what I'm talking about!
That's... great. It would be extremely useful for the case. Obviously.
The skull nods.
You want a spell scroll?
What's the catch?
That'd be useful, yes.
(Hold out your hand.)
The skull widens its jaw. Then it coughs up a tiny spell scroll into the altar.
That's disgusting.
(Grab it.)
(Grab it, reluctantly.)
What is?
You had the scroll inside of yourself.
No I didn't.
It was in my pocket. Clearly.
What are you, stupid? Take the damn scroll!
He is not aware of his demi-lich form.
How sad.
Fascinating more like.
